newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Undone UCB offsets steady PetroFina in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Undone UCB offsets steady PetroFina in Brussels.

text.p: Shares in Bel-20 heavyweight UCB suffered from profit-taking on Tuesday, with dealers an anticipated 30 to 35 percent rise in first half earnings, due on Wednesday, by now fully discounted.

The stock lost 3,900 francs at 140,000. With the share now fully-valued, dealers said some speculative longs had been closed. "It is a case of 'buy on the rumour, sell on the fact' already before the results are out," one trader said.
Blue chip PetroFina ended unchanged at 14,950 francs, down from an intraday high at 15,075, ahead of first half earnings news due on Thursday.
Dealers said a close above 15,000 francs would have been positive, but 14,950 was no significant break below that point. Some already recommended that level as a stop-loss level.

Many rated the share a 'hold' amid concern about future earnings growth. Little inspiring news came from PetroFina's U.S. unit Fina Inc which said late on Monday higher second quarter net profits and earnings per share reflected stronger refining and marketing margins.
But crude oil and natural gas prices were lower, exploration costs higher, and margins for chemicals weaker.
Fina posted net profit of $40.02 million after 38.08 million.
Another featured stock was Union Miniere, down 145 francs at 3,395, paring Monday's sharp gains on dollar strength and higher zinc prices.

A fall in zinc prices as general liquidation rocked an overextended market which saw seven-year highs on Monday, hit UM hard, dealers said. Generale Bank, noting higher zinc prices and dollar strength would at best only be seen in UM's earnings reports with a time lag, rated the stock a 'hold'.
SGB, a major shareholder in Union Miniere, ended down 65 francs at 3,800. Generale Bank said SGB had overreacted to the recent share price rise by UM.
